# Question

Does single-molecule nucleosome patterning at the TSS differ between promoters with
high and low RNA Pol II promoter-proximal pausing, at matched expression?

This began as "highly expressed versus not expressed", but the pausing index is
**undefined for silent genes**: with no nascent transcription both the TSS and the
gene-body window are empty, so the ratio is 0, `Inf` or `NA`. Measured on the exact
pipeline, RHO gives 0/3 reads, GFAP 0/16, NEUROD1 0/0, MYOD1 3/0. Non-expressed genes
are therefore excluded and pausing replaces expression as the axis.

# Where the pausing index comes from

This is the part most easily got wrong, so it is stated explicitly: **the definition
and the data come from two different studies.**

### The definition

Day DS, Zhang B, Stevens SM, *et al.*
"Comprehensive analysis of promoter-proximal RNA polymerase II pausing across mammalian
cell types." *Genome Biology* 2016 Jun 3;17:120.
PMID [27259512](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27259512/);
PMC[4893286](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4893286/);
doi:[10.1186/s13059-016-0984-2](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0984-2).

$$\mathrm{PI}=\frac{\text{TSSR signal}/\text{TSSR width}}{\text{body signal}/\text{body width}},\quad
\text{TSSR}=[-50,+300],\quad \text{body}=[+300,\ \text{TES}+3\,\text{kb}]$$

Two things about that paper matter here. It computes PI from **RNAP2 ChIP-seq** on
hg19/RefSeq, not from nascent-RNA data; and it **publishes no per-gene PI table** —
Additional file 2 is the dataset list, Additional file 3 is GO enrichment of the top and
bottom 25% of genes by PI, Additional file 4 is primers. There is no table to download,
so PI is recomputed here.

### The data actually used

GEO [GSM1480326](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM1480326)
(`GSM1480326_GM12878_GROseq_{plus,minus}.bigWig`), series GSE60454/GSE60456, from

Core LJ, Martins AL, Danko CG, Waters CT, Siepel A, Lis JT.
"Analysis of nascent RNA identifies a unified architecture of initiation regions at
mammalian promoters and enhancers." *Nature Genetics* 2014 Dec;46(12):1311-20.
PMID [25383968](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25383968/);
PMC[4254663](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4254663/);
doi:[10.1038/ng.3142](https://doi.org/10.1038/ng.3142).

This is GM12878 **GRO-seq**, a single replicate, on **hg19** — the companion data to the
`grocap.hg38.GM12878.*` files in the same folder. It is *not* from Day et al. GRO-seq is
the more sensitive assay for pausing; Day et al. say as much about their own ChIP-seq.
Day et al.'s windows are applied to GRO-seq here, so the values are method-comparable
but not numerically identical to that paper.

### Expression

ENCODE [ENCSR820PHH](https://www.encodeproject.org/experiments/ENCSR820PHH/), GM12878
total RNA-seq, GRCh38; RSEM gene quantifications `ENCFF345SHY` (replicate 1) and
`ENCFF873VWU` (replicate 2). Gene IDs are an older GENCODE, so the join to the v46
canonical TSS BED strips the `.version` suffix (58,072 matches version-stripped versus
34,018 with versions).

### Two corrections worth recording

**Assembly.** The GRO-seq is hg19 while the TSS annotation and the Fiber-seq are hg38.
The signal is lifted hg19 to hg38 with `hg19ToHg38.over.chain`; 99.37% of signal is
retained on the worst chromosome (chr22 plus strand), the shortfall being hg19 sequence
with no hg38 counterpart.

**TSS definition dominates PI.** The Ensembl *gene-record* 5' end is not the promoter.
For ACTB the gene record sits 33 kb from the real TSS. PI therefore uses the
`Ensembl_canonical` TSS and the TES of **that same canonical transcript**, joined by
transcript ID.

```{r provenance-table}
data.table(
  item = c("PI definition", "Nascent data", "Expression", "TSS/TES", "Fiber-seq reads"),
  source = c("Day et al. 2016, Genome Biol 17:120 (RNAP2 ChIP-seq, hg19)",
             "Core et al. 2014, Nat Genet 46:1311 / GSM1480326 (GRO-seq, hg19, 1 rep)",
             "ENCODE ENCSR820PHH (GM12878 total RNA-seq, GRCh38, 2 reps)",
             "GENCODE v46 Ensembl_canonical TSS + same-transcript TES (hg38)",
             "31 merged LCL samples, ft extract --m6a (hg38)"))
```

# Method

Nothing scientific is reimplemented. The functions that do the work are sourced
unchanged from the parent pipeline in `..` through `reticulate`:

- `autocorrelations()` from `../03_compute_autocorrelations.py` —
  $\mathrm{ACF}(k)=\sum_t (x_t-\bar x)(x_{t+k}-\bar x)\,/\,(N\operatorname{var}x)$,
  per read, on the unbinned per-base 0/1 m6A signal, at every integer lag. No binning,
  smoothing, tapering, detrending or FFT truncation.
- `repeat_peak()` from `../05_summarize_autocorrelations.py` — strongest positive local
  maximum in 140–250 bp.

Read extraction reuses `assemble_region_m6a()` from
`code/parsing_functions/parsing_footprints_functions.r` with `full_span = TRUE` and an
explicit per-base `positions` vector. Reads are pooled across the 31 LCL samples and are
unphased: pausing is a property of the gene, not of a haplotype.

Windows are TSS-relative and strand-oriented, $[-1000,+1000)$; minus-strand rows are
reversed so column $j$ always holds offset $j-1001$ in the direction of transcription.
The ACF is invariant to that reversal, but the heatmaps are not.

### Choice of statistic

Molecules within one gene share a promoter and are **not** independent, so a
molecule-level test would be anticonservative by thousands of degrees of freedom. The
experimental unit is the gene; the design is matched on expression; the primary test is
therefore a **paired comparison across the matched gene pairs**. The pooled group curves
are descriptive only — they are molecule-weighted, and molecule counts per gene vary
between `r min(rd("read_qc.tsv")$n_reads)` and `r max(rd("read_qc.tsv")$n_reads)`.

# Gene selection

Protein-coding canonical TSSs that are expressed (both replicates > 0, mean TPM ≥ 1),
isolated (no other canonical TSS within ±2 kb), ≥ 4 kb long, with both PI windows
covered, restricted to a 5–60 TPM band, then the top and bottom 2% of PI matched 1:1 on
$\log_{10}$ TPM. The band matters: below ~5 TPM both PI windows are sparse and PI is
counting noise; above ~60 TPM the pool is mostly ribosomal-protein genes with their own
promoter architecture.

```{r regions}
r <- rd("tss_regions.tsv")
r[order(pair, pi_group), .(pair, pi_group, gene = gene_name, chr, tss, strand,
                           mean_tpm = round(mean_tpm, 1), pi = round(pi, 2))]
```

PI is separated about 1000-fold while expression is not (medians
`r round(median(r[pi_group=="high_pi"]$mean_tpm),1)` vs
`r round(median(r[pi_group=="low_pi"]$mean_tpm),1)` TPM, Wilcoxon
p = `r round(wilcox.test(mean_tpm ~ pi_group, data = r)$p.value, 3)`).

# Result

## Primary statistic: paired, per gene

```{r fig-paired, out.width="100%"}
fig("06_paired_comparison.pdf")
```

```{r paired-tests}
rd("paired_tests.tsv")
```

**There is no significant paired difference at this pilot size**, in either phasing
amplitude or repeat length. The amplitude comparison crosses over (3 of 5 evaluable
pairs favour high PI; p = 0.625). The repeat length is the more promising of the two:
it is shorter at high-PI promoters in 4 of 5 pairs, median difference −14 bp, but at
p = 0.125 that is a direction to power up, not a result.

One pair is not evaluable: `repeat_peak()` finds no positive local maximum for DTX4
inside 140–250 bp, because its ACF peaks near 450–500 bp instead.

## Pooled group curves (descriptive only)

```{r fig-group, out.width="100%"}
fig("01_group_mean_acf.pdf")
```

```{r group-peaks}
rd("group_peaks.tsv")[level == "pi_group"]
```

Both groups show clear nucleosome periodicity with a primary peak near 195–199 bp and a
second harmonic near 390 bp. The pooled curves differ in amplitude about three-fold,
**but this gap is not reproduced pair by pair** and should not be read as an effect of
pausing: it reflects between-gene heterogeneity and the unequal molecule counts noted
above. The per-pair panel shows the heterogeneity directly.

```{r fig-pairs, out.width="100%"}
fig("02_per_pair_mean_acf.pdf")
```

## Per-molecule view

```{r fig-heat, out.width="100%"}
fig("03_acf_heatmap.pdf")
```

```{r fig-nrl, out.width="100%"}
fig("05_nrl_per_molecule.pdf")
```

The per-molecule repeat lengths are **uncalibrated**: `repeat_peak()` applies no
prominence constraint, and per-base single-molecule ACF noise is around
$1/\sqrt{2000}\approx0.02$, so a structureless molecule will still return a peak
somewhere in the band. Calibrating this against an A/T-restricted shuffled null is a
genome-wide-stage job.

## The density confound

```{r fig-density, out.width="100%"}
fig("04_m6a_call_fraction.pdf")
```

ACF amplitude depends on m6A density, and density tracks accessibility. Matching on
expression removes most of the expected gap, and what remains runs *against* the pooled
amplitude difference: the low-PI group has slightly **higher** m6A density yet lower
pooled amplitude. The Wilcoxon on that panel is molecule-level and so anticonservative;
treat it as descriptive.

# Read QC

```{r qc}
rd("read_qc.tsv")
```

```{r dropout}
sc <- rd("sample_contribution.tsv")
drop <- sc[, .(regions = .N, zero = sum(overlapping_reads == 0L)),
           by = .(sample_name, chr)][regions == zero]
drop
```

The table above should be empty. Any row in it is a **sample/chromosome dropout**, not
biology.

One such case was found and corrected: `AL6_bc2162_19093.ft_extracted_m6a.chr1.bed.gz`
is **plain gzip rather than BGZF** — the only non-BGZF file among all 775 m6A extracts
(31 samples x 25 chromosomes). A non-BGZF file cannot be tabix-indexed at all, so
htslib returned nothing for every chr1 query and reported it on stderr only, silently
dropping that sample from IPP and DPYD. The data is intact (221,378 records, full chr1
span), so the repair is a lossless recompression rather than a re-index. Because the
shared tree is read-only here, a BGZF copy with byte-identical decompressed content
lives under `LCL_project/fixed_inputs/` and is substituted via
`assemble_region_m6a()`'s `m6a_paths` argument. That restores 7 reads to IPP and 11 to
DPYD, which moves the high-PI pool from 3,358 to 3,376 molecules and changes no
conclusion.

# Caveats

- **GM12878 proxy.** Expression and GRO-seq are both GM12878, so PI and TPM are
  internally consistent, but the Fiber-seq is 31 other LCL donors; GM12878 is not in the
  cohort. A genotype-matched GM12878 Fiber-seq CRAM exists but has no `extracted_results/`,
  so it would need an `ft extract --m6a` pass first.
- **Six pairs.** This is a plumbing-and-direction pilot, not a powered test.
- **Single GRO-seq replicate**, so PI carries no replicate-level error.
- **Day et al. windows on GRO-seq**; GRO-seq pausing indices often use a narrower TSS
  window, worth a sensitivity check.
